day_shape: 63 items: Trump calls off major Iran strike and announces Monday US-Iran talks, CENTCOM reports 35 vessels redirected under Hormuz blockade, IDF blames Hezbollah for Kafra blast wounding 5 LAF soldiers, heavy Araghchi/IRIB messaging cycle.

threads.label: Called-off US strike and reopened Iran talks
threads.summary: Trump announced renewed US-Iran negotiations beginning Monday after calling off what he described as the biggest attack since World War II, with Qatari and Saudi mediation reported. Rubio told Fox News Iran was considering deals on denuclearisation and Hormuz, while a Jerusalem Post report said Israel had been slated to participate in the aborted strike.

threads.label: Hormuz blockade and Oman-mediated passage talks
threads.summary: CENTCOM said its Arabian Sea blockade against Iran had redirected 35 commercial vessels, disabled two and boarded two as of 2 August, with an F-35C flying from USS Abraham Lincoln. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Araghchi said Tehran was negotiating with Oman on safe maritime passage through Hormuz, and Saudi FM Faisal bin Farhan held a call with him on de-escalation.

threads.label: Araghchi framing of 'real war' with US
threads.summary: Foreign Ministry spokesman Araghchi told IRIB Iran is not negotiating with America and is in a real war dating to the 29 Esfand US-Israeli aggression five months prior. IRIB also aired an expert claim putting the US war cost at $200 billion and said two US senators warned CENTCOM that Trump threats to hit Iranian bridges and power plants could be a war crime.

threads.label: Iran executions and juvenile death-row warnings
threads.summary: Iran International reported the judiciary's Mizan agency confirmed two more political prisoners hanged on Monday over alleged Israel intelligence cooperation, and rights groups warned more teenagers detained in January's uprising face imminent execution. Defa Press and IRIB named the two executed men as Omid Behzad and Pooria Safvat, described as Mossad-linked mercenaries who passed coordinates during the 12-day and Ramadan wars.

threads.label: Kafra blast and southern Lebanon operations
threads.summary: The IDF said an explosive device that wounded five Lebanese Armed Forces soldiers in Kafra was planted by Hezbollah, after the LAF initially blamed an Israeli strike and then retracted. Separately the Jerusalem Post reported the 401st Brigade had completed an eight-month southern Lebanon mission, destroying 1,200 Hezbollah structures.

threads.label: Gaza disarmament track and continued IDF strikes
threads.summary: Palestinian Islamic Jihad was reported to have agreed to the Board of Peace disarmament plan, while a Gaza source affiliated with Israeli-backed militias told the Jerusalem Post the plan would not be implemented; BoP head Mladenov implied IDF strikes were interfering with peace efforts. The IDF said recent strikes killed three operatives from three groups in Gaza, and Mohammad Dahlan claimed Kushner assured him Israel would end strikes before deleting the post.

threads.label: Khamenei Arbaeen messaging and Basij commemoration
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted two messages on Arbaeen pilgrimage to Iraq and remembrance of Iran's martyr leader. Defa Press ran Brigadier General Abdollahi's remarks calling the strengthening of the Basij the legacy of Martyr Gholamreza Soleimani, alongside further martyr-commemoration items.

events.title_en: Legal action against exporters who fail to meet currency obligations, says Central Bank
events.summary_en: Exporters who fail to meet their currency obligations after the legal deadline will face legal action. If the amount of unfulfilled currency obligations exceeds 3 million euros, the file will be referred to the prosecutor's office, and if it is less than this amount, it will be sent to the Disciplinary Enforcement Organisation. Bank managers who fail to take necessary legal steps to collect allocated foreign currency will be referred to the disciplinary board of banks.

events.title_en: Charging credits for free food basket for 262 thousand children needing supplementary nutrition
events.summary_en: The Deputy Minister of Welfare and Economic Affairs of the Ministry of Cooperatives, Labour and Social Welfare: From today, a free food basket was charged for over 262 thousand children aged 5 to 59 months needing supplementary nutrition. The credit for purchasing the food basket for malnourished children was increased by 50 per cent in the electronic travel authorisation system in the account of household heads. The amount of the welfare support basket of the Ministry of Welfare for needy families is 2 million tomans and for families with moderate means is 1 million and 200 thousand tomans. Families with children suspected of malnutrition should visit health centres for height and weight monitoring and registration in the system.

events.title: Three terror operatives who were advancing attacks on Israeli troops in the Gaza Strip were killed in recent strikes, the military announces. One strike in Gaza City yesterday killed Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams, a member of the Army of Islam terror group, and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman, a member of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad, according to the IDF. A separate strike last week in the Strip's north killed Ahmad Khudar, a commander in Hamas's Jabalia Battalion, the military says. The IDF justifies the strikes amid the ceasefire by saying that the three terror operatives were advancing attacks, and they were "eliminated in order to remove the threat."

events.title: The Lebanese army says five soldiers were lightly injured by an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon a short while ago. The strike took place in the town of Kafra, while the Lebanese troops were assisting locals, the Lebanese Armed Forces says. There is no immediate comment from the IDF on the incident. Meanwhile, Lebanese media reports a blast in the town of Kounine, apparently as the result of IDF demolition work of Hezbollah infrastructure.
